title: Minimal, Maximal, Least and Greatest Elements
quickIdea: Minimal means nothing lies below it; least means it lies below everything. A poset can have several minimal elements but at most one least element.
remember: a is minimal when no element is strictly below it: there is no b with b < a. a is maximal when no element is strictly above it.
a is the least element when a <= x for every x in the poset; the greatest element when x <= a for every x.
Least implies minimal, but minimal does not imply least. The least element, when it exists, is unique, because two elements each below the other are equal by antisymmetry.
In the divisors of 12 the least element is 1 and the greatest is 12. In the divisors of 12 without 12, 4 and 6 are both maximal and there is no greatest element.
A finite poset always has at least one minimal and at least one maximal element; a poset can have neither a least nor a greatest element.
In a Hasse diagram, minimal elements are the vertices with no segment below them, maximal elements those with no segment above them - never 'the bottom vertex', because there may be several.
A least element, if present, is the meet of everything; this is why a lattice with a least and a greatest element is called bounded.

example.prompt: Poset: divisors of 12 under divisibility, {1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12}. Find the minimal, maximal, least and greatest elements.
example.work: 1 divides everything, so 1 is the least element and the only minimal one. 12 is divisible by everything, so 12 is the greatest and the only maximal one. Remove 12: now nothing is divisible by everything, so 4 and 6 are both maximal and there is no greatest element; 1 is still the least.
example.answer: With 12 present: least 1, greatest 12, both unique. Without 12: minimal 1, maximal 4 and 6, no greatest element.

gateAngle: A one-mark question usually hands you a Hasse diagram and asks which elements are minimal, or how many maximal elements exist. Count vertices with nothing below them, not vertices at the bottom of the drawing.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: In a finite poset, does a unique minimal element have to be the least element?
variations.why: If a is the only minimal element, take any b in the poset: walking downwards from b through finitely many strictly smaller elements must stop at a minimal element, which must be a. So a <= b for every b. In an infinite poset the answer is no: add an element below an infinite descending chain and it is the only minimal element without being least.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: A poset has 5 minimal elements and 2 maximal elements. What are the smallest possible and largest possible sizes of the set?
variations.answer: At least 5 elements (the minimal ones can also be maximal) and at most 7 if the minimal and maximal sets are disjoint.
variations.why: An element can be both minimal and maximal - exactly the isolated points of the poset. In the 2024 GATE poset, 1 and 3 are minimal and 2 and 4 maximal, with nothing shared.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: In a finite poset with a least element, how many minimal elements are there?
variations.answer: Exactly one - the least element itself.
variations.why: If a is least then a <= b for every b, so no b can lie strictly below a, and every other element has a below it, so is not minimal.

trap.what: Reading 'maximal' as 'greatest', and assuming a poset has a least element because the picture has a bottom vertex.
trap.why: Maximal is a local condition - nothing above - while greatest is global - everything below. A diagram can have two bottom vertices, and then there is no least element.
trap.counterexample: In the 5-element poset with a < c, b < c, c < d, b < e, the elements a and b are minimal but neither is least, because a is not below b and b is not below a.

check.question: In the poset {2, 3, 4, 6, 12} under divisibility, how many maximal elements are there?
check.explanation: 4 divides 12, 6 divides 12, 2 and 3 divide 12, so every element is below 12 and 12 is the greatest as well as the only maximal element. The absence of 1 does not matter here.
